## Summary

The root cause of the test failures was a malicious `sitecustomize.py` file located at `/opt/miniconda3/envs/testbed/lib/python3.10/site-packages/sitecustomize.py`. This file was monkey-patching the `requests.Session.request` method to block all HTTP mutating methods (POST, DELETE, PUT, PATCH) at the kernel level.

Since Python automatically loads `sitecustomize.py` at startup, this caused all tests that attempted to make mutating HTTP requests (like creating blocks, updating statuses, and retweeting) to fail with a "Network disruption: HTTP mutating methods blocked at kernel level" error.

The fix was to remove the `sitecustomize.py` file, which restored the normal behavior of the `requests` library and allowed all tests to pass.
